ds: Coercive collection of 'protection' money or repayments on high-interest illegal loans by organised crime groups, usually from small businesses and vulnerable individuals. Victims often show regular payments that do not match any invoice or service, sometimes via third parties or cash.

src.t: UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (2000)
UNODC, public material on organised crime and extortion
Europol, European Union Serious and Organised Crime Threat Assessment (EU SOCTA) (specify year, e.g. 2021 or 2025)

cn.rt: Victims pay protection or loan-shark money from personal accounts, with coerced cash withdrawals, accompanied visits and collector accounts; personal loans taken to pay.

rat: Regular unexplained payments and cash withdrawals by small businesses/vulnerable victims.

ind.n: Regular fixed payments from a small business to an individual with no invoices
ind.cx: Payments at regular intervals to a person or company with no service provided.
ind.ds: Payments at regular intervals to a person or company with no service provided.

ind.n: Sudden cash withdrawals followed by pay-outs under apparent pressure
ind.cx: Customer withdraws cash and appears distressed or accompanied.
ind.ds: Customer withdraws cash and appears distressed or accompanied.

ind.n: High-interest informal loans with repayments to non-lender individuals
ind.cx: Repeated payments with high effective interest rates and rollovers.
ind.ds: Repeated payments with high effective interest rates and rollovers.

ind.n: Collector accounts receiving many payments from unrelated small payers
ind.cx: Single account collects from many businesses in a locality.
ind.ds: A single account receives payments from numerous unrelated senders with no evident commercial or family link to the holder.
ind.cn: Account collecting funds from many unrelated payers

ind.n: Businesses closing or reporting threats alongside payment spikes
ind.cx: Sector-wide complaints in area linked to payments.
ind.ds: Sector-wide complaints in area linked to payments.

ind.n: Use of third-party couriers or intermediaries to collect cash
ind.cx: Cash picked up by runners; multiple deposits by apparent intermediaries.
ind.ds: Cash picked up by runners; multiple deposits by apparent intermediaries.

ind.n: Associates linked to known organised crime groups
ind.cx: Counterparties in adverse media or law enforcement intelligence.
ind.ds: Counterparties, suppliers, respondents or controllers appear in adverse media, law-enforcement notices or intelligence connected to financial crime, abuse, forced labour or organised crime.
ind.cn: Adverse media or intelligence linking counterparties to criminal activity

ind.n: Forced purchase of services, supplies or cars at inflated prices
ind.cx: Businesses pay inflated invoices to specific suppliers.
ind.ds: Businesses pay inflated invoices to specific suppliers.

ctl.ds: Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

Provides discreet escalation routes and private conversation procedures so staff can refer suspected victims of exploitation, coercion or trafficking to specialists, police and support organisations. It prioritises victim safety.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

Translates published and sanitised typologies and red flags into targeted monitoring scenarios and context-aware rules that are reviewed periodically. It aligns monitoring with known criminal methods.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.

ctl.n: Cash exchange, declaration and courier checks
ctl.ds: Collects identification for cash exchange, cross-checks cross-border cash declarations, screens freight, mail and cash-in-transit use and applies courier intelligence. It addresses bulk cash movement across borders.
Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.

Investigates linked clusters and networks of accounts as one case, including broker networks and accounts connected to seizures or requests, rather than reviewing accounts individually. It disrupts organised activity that single-account review would miss.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.
